final_state.job_description:
AI Software Engineering Intern

We're looking for an AI Software Engineering Intern to join our team building
LLM-powered applications and data-driven tools. You'll work on retrieval-
augmented generation systems, custom AI agents, and full-stack applications
that put them in front of real users.

Responsibilities:
- Develop AI applications using Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-
  Augmented Generation (RAG), and custom agent-based workflows
- Build and contribute to full-stack web applications, working across both
  frontend and backend
- Perform data analysis and preprocessing to support AI-driven features
- Apply deep learning techniques to real-world signal/data problems
- Collaborate with a multidisciplinary engineering team on AI-driven solutions
- Write clean, maintainable Python code and contribute to system design

Requirements:
- Currently pursuing or holding a degree in Computer Science, Computer
  Engineering, or a related field
- Strong programming skills in Python; familiarity with Java, C++, or
  JavaScript a plus
- Coursework or hands-on experience with Deep Learning and/or Large
  Language Models
- Experience with Git/GitHub and collaborative development workflows
- Comfortable with data structures, database systems, and SQL
- Strong communication skills and ability to work across disciplines

Nice to have:
- Experience implementing RAG pipelines or LLM-based agents
- Exposure to full-stack development (HTML/CSS, databases, backend frameworks)
- Familiarity with basic cybersecurity concepts or infrastructure tools
- Prior project or internship experience applying deep learning to real data
  (e.g. signal processing, anomaly detection)

This is an internship position with mentorship from senior engineers, ideal
for someone looking to grow their AI/ML and software engineering skills on
real production systems.

questions: Can you explain how you implemented Python in your projects, such as your SigmaTutor or Heartbeat Anomaly Detection, and walk me through your technical approach?

Given that SQL and database systems are a core requirement for our data-driven tools, can you describe a time you designed a database schema or wrote complex queries using SQL, and how you ensured data integrity?
Tell me about a time you had to learn a new AI framework or tool quickly under pressure for your STEM Outreach Program or your recent internship at Dar, and what your approach was.
Walk me through your role as an AI & Software Engineering Intern at Dar this past Summer 2026, and highlight your key contributions to LLM-powered applications or RAG systems during that time.

During our discussion, we noted a discrepancy regarding your experience with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), as your CV lists this skill while your interview responses indicated that you have not yet learned it; could you help clarify your current level of familiarity and hands-on experience with RAG?
answers: he most complex thing I've built with Python is the Heartbeat Anomaly Detection project. I cleaned and segmented ECG signals with NumPy and Pandas, then trained a deep learning model in PyTorch to classify abnormal beats, evaluating it with precision and recall because abnormal beats are rare.

In the Camp Management System, I designed a relational schema with separate tables for participants, camps, registrations, and schedules, linked with foreign keys. I wrote SQL queries with JOINs to list each camper's schedule, GROUP BY queries to count registrations per camp, and I used parameterized queries in the backend to prevent SQL injection.
Honestly, I have never learned RAG. At Dar I mostly worked on full-stack features and data analysis, not AI pipelines

At Dar I worked with the engineering team on internal full-stack tools. I built frontend pages and backend endpoints, and did data analysis and preprocessing on project data. I also got exposure to cybersecurity through Microsoft Defender and the ICT infrastructure team.
Sorry, I misspoke. I implemented the RAG pipeline for SigmaTutor myself, including chunking the course materials, embedding them, and retrieving the relevant sections for the LLM.

Describes contributions to full-stack tools, backend endpoints, data preprocessing, and cybersecurity exposure, satisfying full-stack and multidisciplinary team collaboration requirements.

Clarifies the previous contradiction by stating they did implement a RAG pipeline for SigmaTutor with chunking, embeddings, and retrieval, but the initial misstatement and subsequent correction introduces some uncertainty regarding the depth of hands-on experience.
